lines.trans: Max, we are all very proud of you today.
I am not the hero, Ainura cooked the pilaf.
Sergey Fyodorovich, what are you doing in here?
Dima, what else is left for me now?
I lost all my money, I am completely bankrupt.
Wait, who are you? Are you bankrupt too?
You see, without money nobody needs me anymore.
Yes, now I see that very well.
Listen, why did you not go home?

examples.trans: Every single kopeck of ours was there.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Конечно, нашему ресторану нужен хороший хозяин.
examples.trans: Of course, our restaurant needs a good owner.

examples.text: Хозяин должен быть сильный и уверенный.
examples.trans: The owner must be strong and confident.

examples.text: А почему я должен прийти с Катей?
examples.trans: And why should I come with Katya?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'children' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: This is my child.

examples.text: Ребёнок спит.
examples.trans: The child is asleep.

examples.text: Да! Даже ребёнок знает.
examples.trans: Yes! Even a child knows.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'круг').

examples.text: Там жена и дети вокруг тебя ходят.
examples.trans: Your wife and children walk around you there.

examples.text: Она вокруг меня бегала.
examples.trans: She was running after me (around me).

examples.text: Посмотри вокруг.
examples.trans: Look around.

ходить.gloss: to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)

meanings.en: to walk, to go on foot
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)'.

examples.text: По всем признакам всё сходится.
examples.trans: By all the signs, everything adds up.

examples.text: По признакам всё точно сходится.
examples.trans: By the signs, everything matches up.

examples.text: Ребята, что у вас тут вообще происходит?
examples.trans: Guys, what on earth is going on in here?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rejoice, be glad', paired with 'обрадоваться'.

examples.text: И вся его семья радуется!
examples.trans: And his whole family is thrilled!

examples.text: Дети радовались первому снегу.
examples.trans: The children rejoiced at the first snow.

examples.text: Не радуйся раньше времени.
examples.trans: Do not celebrate too early.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Там все дома радуются и весело смеются.
examples.trans: Everyone at home rejoices and laughs merrily there.

examples.text: Он бегает и очень весело играет.
examples.trans: He runs around and plays very merrily.

examples.text: Шеф, почему вы так весело улыбаетесь?
examples.trans: Chef, why are you smiling so cheerfully?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'меяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to laugh', paired with 'засмеяться'.

examples.text: Не смейся!
examples.trans: Don't laugh!

examples.text: Дети смеются.
examples.trans: The children are laughing.

examples.text: Не смейся. Диктуй номер.
examples.trans: Don't laugh. Read me the number.
